    "For Success (binary outcome), use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as predictor or a generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with binomial link, including Mouse as random effect",
    "Given severe imbalance in paradigm frequencies (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505 and Bright Visual Only n=3323), apply weighted or unweighted analysis with careful interpretation of variance heterogeneity",

    "For Success (logistic/GLMM), use estimated marginal means with multiplicity-adjusted comparisons (e.g., Tukey-adjusted odds ratios)",
    "Prioritize hypothesis-driven contrasts: Combined vs each unimodal condition (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and Combined vs Sham to assess multisensory integration effects; Sham vs all active conditions to assess stimulation efficacy",
    "Report effect sizes (η² for ANOVA, Cohen's h or odds ratios for Success, Cohen's d for pairwise contrasts) alongside p-values"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Control family-wise error rate (FWER) across the 10 pairwise comparisons within each response variable using Tukey's method; for multiplicity across the 5 response variables, consider hierarchical testing with ANOVA F-test gatekeeping or Bonferroni-adjusted significance level (α = 0.01) for exploratory analysis. Additionally, control false discovery rate (FDR using Benjamini-Hochberg) as sensitivity analysis given large sample size and correlated outcomes.",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Stimulation paradigm is categorical with 5 unordered levels, making it inappropriate for ordinary linear regression with paradigm treated as continuous. RECOMMEND: Multinomial logistic regression (softmax regression) or multinomial probit model to predict Stim Paradigm from the five performance variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD). Include Mouse as random effects if using mixed multinomial logistic regression. Alternatively, use Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) or Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) if multivariate normality holds, or Random Forest for non-parametric classification. Given substantial class imbalance (Combined: 63.7%, ICMS Only: 14.8%, Dim Visual Only: 12.5%, Sham: 4.6%, Bright Visual Only: 4.3%), apply class weights, stratified sampling, or balanced accuracy metrics to prevent prediction dominated by Combined paradigm. Evaluate with stratified cross-validation and report confusion matrices, per-class precision/recall, and macro-averaged F1.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: QQ plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals of continuous outcomes; given n=76655, normality of residuals may be assumed by CLT but check for extreme skewness (Path Efficiency, Time-to-Target show long right tails)",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test across 5 paradigms; expected violation due to wide SD ranges and paradigm-specific variability",
    "Independence: Assess within-mouse correlation; Mixed models may be required given repeated measures from 8 mice (~9000-12000 trials per mouse)",
    "Multicollinearity: Check correlations among 5 predictors for multinomial model (e.g., Speed and Time-to-Target likely inversely correlated)",
    "Complete separation check for Success logistic regression: verify no paradigm has 0% or 100% success rate"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined paradigm expected to show superior performance: fastest Time-to-Target, highest Success rate, highest Path Efficiency, and lowest AD due to multisensory integration benefits",
    "ICMS Only and visual-only paradigms (Dim, Bright) expected to perform intermediately, with possible differences between Dim and Bright Visual depending on visibility conditions",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: slowest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, lowest Path Efficiency, highest AD reflecting spatial uncertainty without stimulation guidance",
    "Average Speed may show less paradigm differentiation as mice maintain similar locomotor speeds regardless of target locatability",
    "Large sample in Combined vs small samples in Sham and Bright Visual Only will yield high power for Combined contrasts but imprecise estimates for rare paradigms"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance: Combined (63.7%) vastly overrepresented versus Sham (4.6%) and Bright Visual Only (4.3%), causing unstable variance estimates and reduced power for rare paradigms in ANOVA and predictive modeling",
    "Outliers and extreme values: Path Efficiency SD (0.47) >> mean (0.47) with max 29.8; Time-to-Target max 201.4 >> mean 2.8, indicating heavy right tails and potential non-normality; Winsorization or transformation may be needed",
    "Success is binary but highly imbalanced across paradigms (mean 0.73, SD 0.44); logistic models may face quasi-complete separation in small paradigms",
    "Missing randomization details and trial-level correlation structure unknown; assumed independence within Mouse may understate uncertainty",
    "No information on trial order, learning effects, or session structure; temporal confounds possible",
    "Summary-only data view precludes trial-level stratification or temporal analysis; aggregate statistics may mask individual trial variability"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a multinomial logistic mixed-effects model predicting Stim Paradigm from the five standardized performance metrics with Mouse as random intercept, using class weights to address imbalance. Simultaneously, conduct a permutational MANOVA (PERMANOVA) on the multivariate performance space to test overall paradigm differences without normality assumptions. Validate predictive model with stratified 10-fold cross-reporting balanced accuracy, and if separation issues arise in binary Success models, use Firth's penalized logistic regression or Bayesian methods with regularizing priors."
}
